children: Himanshi Lohchab & Tanya Pandey Mumbai | New Delhi: A surge in cyberattacks on Indian organisations including State Bank of India, Central Bank of India, Bharat Electronics and hundreds of NBFCs has triggered a wave of cyber insurance claims, with insurers facing estimated losses of thousands of crores over the next few months.

While businesses rush to enhance their cyber insurance cover, the incidents have triggered a debate over whether existing policies adequately cover emerging cyber risks. The biggest question insurers are policyholders seem to be confronting is: who pays when a vulnerability exposes thousands of organisations to the same threat? Cyber insurance typically covers everything from costs of forensic audits, data breaches and business interruption to ransomware losses. In some instances, insurers even directly negotiate with the hacker to determine whether and how much ransom needs to be paid. There's also an uncertainty surrounding attacks involving rogue AI agents.

title: Cyberattacks Put Insurance Firewall to Test
